title: Epochal CUDA-Graph transactionalization and replay-fencing for multi-stream decode stability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: We observe non-deterministic stalls and occasional token corruption during concurrent multi-stream decode when CUDA Graph capture and replay interleave with prefill KV updates. This ticket aims to implement an 'epochal' transactionalization for CUDA Graph captures and bounded replay-fencing so replays are applied only against compatible KV/cache epochs. Goals: 1) Guarantee replay correctness across interleaved prefill+decode workflows. 2) Prevent partial-replay races that cause token duplication or dropped tokens. 3) Keep end-to-end latency impact <5% p95 for typical chat workloads. 4) Add deterministic validation tests and synthetic workloads for CI.
background: Current state: The serving runtime captures CUDA Graphs per decode path, but when prefill updates KV caches for other streams, subsequent replays can observe mismatched internal allocator/state leading to incorrect kernel binding or stale KV indexes. Previous heuristics (forced synchronization, global mutexes) reduced incidence but caused severe throughput regressions. Related issues: complexity increases with kernel-selection heuristics that choose different fused attention kernels depending on sequence length distribution. We need a solution that composes with existing kernel-selection and batching strategies.
proposal: Introduce an epoch token (numeric identifier) on graph capture metadata and on KV/prefill checkpoints. Each capture will be tagged with the active epoch. On replay, validate the capture epoch against the current KV epoch for the target stream. If mismatch: 1) fast-fallback to a safe non-graph decode path for that request, or 2) trigger a deterministic recapture if sufficient warmup tokens and resource constraints allow. Implement lightweight per-GPU epoch counters and a 'fence' operation that ensures captures that depend on a given KV epoch are replayed only while that epoch is still valid. Expose a configurable policy: conservative (fallback) vs aggressive (recapture).
acceptance_criteria: 1) No token corruption or duplication under synthetic adversarial test that interleaves prefill updates and decode replays at high concurrency (1000 concurrent streams) across 4 GPUs. 2) Perf regression: p95 latency increase <=5% on existing decode benchmark, throughput change <=7% for steady-state chat profile. 3) CI deterministic test added that reproduces previous failure and shows fixed behavior. 4) Metric dashboards: incident rate for 'graph-replay-mismatch' must drop to <1 per 100k decode requests after rollout. 5) Feature flag gate to disable epoch enforcement per deployment.
implementation_notes: - Add epoch counter to graph metadata struct (64-bit). Avoid extra CUDA memcpys on hot path; store epoch in host-side capture table and pass via lightweight device pinned memory when needed. - When prefill completes, increment KV epoch for the target stream/pool and mark any dependent captures as stale. - Replay code path checks epoch; on mismatch, call policy handler. - Recapture workflow must be gated by a capture budget and backoff to avoid thundering-herd. - Integrate with kernel-selection: recapture should re-run kernel selection pass with current sequence distribution to ensure chosen kernels match runtime conditions. - Add observability: histogram of epoch skew, counter of fallbacks, recapture latency distribution. - Ensure compatibility with Dedicated mode where GPU pools are long-lived and with Private deployments where pinned memory semantics may differ.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests: epoch tagging/validation logic, fence semantics. 2) Integration tests: small-scale multi-stream harness with deterministic scheduler to validate playback vs. prefill ordering. 3) Stress tests: fuzzing harness that randomly orders prefill and decode operations across GPUs and checks token-level equality with a ground-truth single-threaded decoder. 4) End-to-end perf test in staging with chat workload (seq distributions) to measure overhead. 5) Canary rollout: enable on 5% of traffic with verbose logging and auto-rollback thresholds.
rollout_and_mitigation: - Roll out behind a feature flag and default policy conservative (fallback to non-graph decode). - Phase 1: staging run with offline traffic replay for 48h. Phase 2: 5% canary for 24h, monitor 'fallback' and 'recapture' rates and latency. Phase 3: gradual increase to 50% if metrics stable. - If fallback rate >0.5% or p95 latency regresses >10%, rollback flag. - Post-mortem plan: capture full trace, graph capture metadata, and kernel-selection logs for failing requests.
metrics_and_dashboards: Key metrics to add: graph_replay_mismatch_count, graph_capture_epoch_skew_histogram, graph_fallback_count, graph_recapture_count, recapture_duration_p50_p95. Add alert: graph_replay_mismatch_count > 10/hour on prod. Dashboard links: https://dash.redwood.internal/runtime/graph-epochs (placeholder).
risks: 1) Extra synchronization could reintroduce contention if not designed as non-blocking. 2) Frequent recaptures may reduce throughput; need effective backoff. 3) Interaction with kernel-selection: recapture may pick different kernels causing cache churn. 4) Complexity of cross-GPU epoch consistency in multi-tenant Dedicated hosts.
